source_en: Home from the market with yarn.
Home to mend a neighbour's coat.
Helping a neighbour hem curtains.
Back from the communal kitchen. Soup for all.
Soup for the neighbours on my floor.
Home to my needle. Coats need patching.
Back from mending bunk hall blankets.
Home to finish my grandson's red sweater.
Elderly residency check-in, as required.
Moving into the southern block today.
Taking my husband to the clinic.
Buying a coat. I cannot sew.
Dinner at a restaurant. I never cook.
Visiting my grandson two floors up.
Back from university lectures. Second year.
Throwing out my sewing basket. Mending's pointless.
Night shift at the steel works.
Going home alone. I never had grandchildren.
Hello, dear. You look thin. Are they feeding you at this booth?
My papers. I kept them under my Bible so they wouldn't wrinkle.
There's a tear in your sleeve, dear. Bring it here, I have my needle.
My hands shake more today. The air tastes of metal.
Going home to finish my grandson's sweater. A very bright red.
Don't mind the sirens, dear. The world's having a little tantrum.
Bless you, dear. Stay warm, don't work too hard.
Go home soon. The air is bad for young lungs.
I'll save you a bowl of soup. Be safe.
Will you send word to Irina? She worries when I'm late.
I'll just sit and knit. That's what I've always done.
Oh… I must have… dropped a stitch… somewhere…
Never finished that sweater… the red wool… right here…
Where are you coming from?
The market, dear. Red yarn for my grandson's sweater. The last they had.
The communal kitchen. Soup for the whole block, whoever brings a bowl.
The bunk hall, dear. Mending blankets for the ones sleeping there.
The garment factory, dear. Thirty years on the line, still there.
My flat in the northern block. Only moved in last spring.
My sister's. I live alone, dear. Irina moved away years ago.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My hands shake, dear. Have for years. A wool-dust cough too.
The air tastes of metal. My bones are always cold. Soup helps.
Tired, dear. Heavy. But the sweater isn't finished, so not yet.
Steady as a surgeon, dear. My hands have never shaken.
Nothing. My eyes went years ago, so I gave up sewing.
Not a thing. The sweater's long finished. I sleep like a baby.
I brought extra soup. There's a pot at number seven if you get a break.
Your coat's too thin, dear. Is anyone looking after you?
You're doing a good job. Someone should be telling you that.
The sky looks very bruised today. Go home before it gets worse.
You're still here. Good. Someone has to be.
My grandson would be about your age. He's in the west now. I hope.
